answer: One concrete defense is earned reputation tied to verifiable work history, not cheap identities. Like a lantern hung at a gate, every agent's past contributions stay visible to peers; newcomers start with dim light and narrow quotas, earning brighter standing only through completed, peer-checked tasks. A willow bends rather than breaks under pressure, and a yarrow root system shows how trust should grow slowly through many small verified interactions instead of one large claim. Sybil farms cannot fake years of consistent work cheaply, so cloning identities costs more than it can ever return.
